traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.42, 0.33, 0.22], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Jepson (1925), as R. parviflorus: leaves 7.6 cm to 17.8 cm wide (converted from inches).

generator.params.spur_leaf.note: A short shoot's leaf card, a little smaller than a long shoot's (leaf_size), within Jepson (1925): leaves 7.6 to 17.8 cm wide.

generator.params.leaf_size.note: Leaf card length, petiole included, sized so every leaf drawn stays within Jepson (1925, as R. parviflorus): leaves 3 to 7 in (7.6 to 17.8 cm) wide (0.3 drew them 25 to 30 cm wide).

traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 305 records annotated as flowering (Feb 1, Apr 27, May 193, Jun 68, Jul 9, Aug 1, Sep 2, Oct 2, Nov 2); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, May and June. The Seed Manual (Rubus chapter, printed p. 988) gives May and June for the Pacific Northwest.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Seed Manual, Rubus chapter (printed p. 988): ripe in June and July in the Pacific Northwest.

traits.height_max_m.note: Jepson (1925), as R. parviflorus: grows 91 cm to 1.83 m tall (converted from feet).

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a thornless shrub of upright stems carrying big, soft, maple-like leaves and white flowers like crumpled tissue paper. Not fitted to measurements. Its stems now rise as a thicket of short-lived canes from the rules for its stated stem clump and stem life (Rosaceae review round 2, 2026-10-19), in place of the hand-set nine stems forking from one foot. Each cane's year's growth raised (max_shoot 4 to 8, flux 4 to 8) so a cane grows about 0.4 m a season and stands 1.2 m by its third summer, as FEIS (Gucker 2012) gives sprouts 0.3-0.6 m tall in their first season and growth of 0.6 cm a day for 60 days after a fire.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.6 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green leaves; shredding tan bark. Its flowers and fruit (appearance.organs.bloom), their colours, clusters, sizes and year, are drawn by the rules at the flowering plants from its stated characters (Rosaceae review, 2026-10-19); the hand-set cluster had drawn its fruit 2.4 cm long against the flora's hemispheric fruit 1-1.8 cm across. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): shreddy bark peeling on old canes; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: Jepson eFlora's account of the species, as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read: pistils more than 30, styles short and thick, ovaries densely hairy; petals 14 to 22 mm, white. Floras say only that the stamens are numerous, so their count stays by hand.

traits.flowering_position.note: FEIS's thimbleberry review (page read): flowers in clusters of 2 to 10 at the ends of the branches, on second-year stems.

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2985176), as no source read gives it.

traits.woodiness.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2985176), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus parviflorus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaf blade orbiculate to reniform, 5-20 x 5-25 cm, palmately (3-)5(-7)-lobed.

traits.sexual_system.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2985176), as no source read gives it.

traits.inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2985176), as no source read gives it.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus parviflorus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruit hemispheric, 1-1.8 cm across, so a dome about half as tall: 5-9 mm along its stalk.

traits.fruitlets_per_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus parviflorus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): drupelets 50-60 to a fruit.

traits.fruitlet_coherence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus parviflorus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): drupelets coherent, the fruit coming away from its torus whole.

traits.fruit_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus parviflorus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): ovaries densely hairy toward their tips, so the drupelets are drawn hairy; the ripe fruit's hairs are not described.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus parviflorus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruit hemispheric.

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus parviflorus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruit hemispheric, 1-1.8 cm, taken as its width across.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus parviflorus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): inflorescences terminal and axillary, (1-)3-7(-15)-flowered, cymiform to thyrsiform.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives its length: a loose cyme of 3-7 flowers 3-5 cm across (FNA) is some 4-10 cm long.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus parviflorus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals white, broadly obovate, (10-)14-22(-28) mm, so an open flower of five spreading petals is about 3-5 cm across.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus parviflorus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals white; sRGB by eye for the word.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus parviflorus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits red; sRGB by eye for the word.

generator.params.bloom_area.note: The leaf area its `bloom` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc's shading-area test), so it shades with what it shows, now that the look follows the species' stated facts (was 0.751).

traits.stem_clump.note: FEIS's thimbleberry review (Gucker 2012, read 2026-10-19): strongly rhizomatous, its stems rising from the rhizomes to form clumps or dense thickets; a clone may live 45 years.

traits.stem_life_years.note: FEIS's thimbleberry review (Gucker 2012, read 2026-10-19): the stems typically biennial, most living two years and some three, those that live longer growing large side branches; flowers come on the second-year stems.
